There are three perspectives, 1st, 2nd, & 3rd person.

In geometry it would be the dot (no axis, single point of reference), the line connecting two dots (X-axis, two reference points), and the triangle (X&Y axes, three or more reference points. These are, respectively, one dimensional, two dimensional, and three dimensional objects.

In video games, cinematography, and narrative work the first person (dot, no axis) perspective is from the point of view of the main character. Think FPS games, autobiographies or when the narrator is the main character, or movies like the Blair Witch project.

The second person perspective (line, x-axis) is much more rare. Because it faces the main character, directly. Examples would be a portrait or a mirror. We are trained on the face and features of the main character but we are not seeing through their eyes. In a two person dialogue, we experience the other in the second-person perspective.

The third person perspective (triangle, x & y axes) is possibly the most commonly used in art. It is the "fly on the wall" or the "bird's eye view." Here, we observe two (or more) entities interacting with one another. We are non-participants (excepting the Observer's Effect.) Examples are games like Zelda, movies like Avengers, books where the narrator is not a character in the plot (like Harry Potter.) When a character in a story speaks to the audience, they are "breaking the fourth wall." Because the third reference point is the camera, but the fourth is the person who is looking at a screen or sheet of paper.
